name: Sify Technologies Limited
one_line: Indian ICT and hyperscale data centre operator running NVIDIA-certified AI-ready campuses and the CloudInfinit +AI GPU cloud.
notes: Sify's own release names Chennai, Noida and Navi Mumbai as NVIDIA DGX-Ready certified campuses supporting H100, H200, B200, GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 at up to 130 kW/rack. It advertises hourly pay-per-use colocation but publishes no rate card, so no hourly price is recorded. NASDAQ-listed, so 20-F/6-K filings should be treated as T1 over website copy.

name: E2E Networks Limited
one_line: Listed Indian GPU cloud provider selling NVIDIA H100/H200/B200 capacity by the hour from Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru.
notes: Published on-demand USD per-GPU-hour rates as of this capture: B200 $6.50, H200 $3.49, H100 $2.90, RTX PRO 6000 $1.90, A100 80GB $2.10, A100 40GB $1.98, A40 $1.44, A30 $1.35, L40S $1.20, L4 $0.57 (ex-tax, per-minute billing). A separate third-party comparison dated Feb 2026 quotes INR rates H200 Rs183/hr and H100 Rs175/hr, which do not reconcile with the USD card; both are recorded but the company page is the stronger source. NSE-listed.

name: Yotta Data Services Private Limited
one_line: Hiranandani-backed Indian hyperscale data centre and sovereign GPU cloud operator; runs Shakti Cloud out of Navi Mumbai and Greater Noida.
notes: IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: Yotta Data Services (India, yotta.com, Shakti Cloud) is NOT the same company as 'Yotta Labs' (yottalabs.ai), a separate GPU marketplace that publishes its own USD rate card. Do not merge. Yotta Data Services does not publish a public hourly rate card; third-party surveys list it as quote-only.

name: NeevCloud
one_line: Indian AI cloud selling NVIDIA GPU clusters by the hour with India-hosted infrastructure.
notes: Published H200 rates (INR per GPU-hour): Rs231.17 on-demand, Rs192.48 on 3-month commit, Rs184.74 on 6-month, Rs179.91 on 1-year. Price includes 20 vCPU, 192GB RAM, ephemeral NVMe, InfiniBand. States '100% India-Hosted' but names no city, so hq_city left null.

name: Jarvislabs.ai
one_line: Indian GPU cloud renting NVIDIA GPUs by the hour to ML developers, billed in USD outside India and INR inside.
notes: Published on-demand USD per-GPU-hour: H200 SXM $3.99, H100 SXM $2.69, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell $1.89, A100 80GB $1.49, A100 40GB $0.89, A30 $0.41, L4 $0.44. Site states customers outside India are billed in USD. A separate Indian comparison lists Jarvis Labs at Rs270/hr for H100 and Rs100/hr for A100, which does not reconcile with the USD card at any plausible FX rate; both recorded, company page preferred.

name: Neysa
one_line: Indian AI cloud offering GPU-as-a-Service and inference on NVIDIA and AMD accelerators via its Velocis platform.
notes: Own blog publishes Neysa rates in INR per hour: H100 SXM 80GB Rs275, H200 141GB Rs200, L40S 48GB Rs100, L4 24GB Rs74.8, H100 fractional (10GB) Rs40. The H200 rate being below the H100 SXM rate is unusual and may reflect a promotional or fractional SKU; flagged rather than corrected. About page claims 'backed by over $1Bn in funding' naming Blackstone and OTPP among investors; HQ city not stated on the page so left null.

name: AceCloud
one_line: Indian cloud provider renting NVIDIA GPUs by the hour in INR.
notes: Published INR per-GPU-hour rates dated Feb 2026: H100 HGX Rs315.07, A100 Rs184.93, L40S Rs123.29, RTX 6000 Ada Rs84.28, A30 Rs71.92, RTX A6000 Rs59.08, L4 Rs41.92, A2 Rs23.01. Page itself warns rates vary with FX and data centre region.

name: Krutrim
one_line: Ola-founded Indian AI company offering GPU-as-a-service and sovereign cloud on NVIDIA hardware.
notes: No public hourly rate card found: listing page states 'Price Available on Request'. HQ city Bengaluru taken from the Ola launch coverage, not from a filing.

name: Tata Communications Limited
one_line: Indian carrier and cloud operator offering GPU cloud capacity to Indian enterprises on request.
notes: Third-party survey records Tata Communications as INR-billed with 'pricing on request' and no published hourly rate. No first-party GPU rate card verified in this pass; treat capacity claims as unconfirmed until an NSE filing is checked.

name: CtrlS Datacenters Limited
one_line: Indian rated-4 data centre operator building large AI-capable campuses in Telangana and other Indian metros.
notes: Reported as already operating three Hyderabad data centres of 4MW to 13MW before the Chandanvelly campus. No GPU rate card published.

name: Cyfuture India Private Limited
one_line: Indian cloud and data centre provider marketing AI/GPU cloud services.
notes: GPU pricing page returned 404 during this capture; no published hourly rate verified. HQ Noida is from company self-description on the cited blog, not a filing.

name: Reliance Intelligence
one_line: Reliance's AI arm, building a gigawatt-scale sovereign AI compute backbone at Jamnagar on NVIDIA GB300.
notes: Jio, Reliance Jio, Reliance Intelligence and Digital Connexion (Reliance/Brookfield/Digital Realty JV) are related but distinct vehicles; the Jamnagar AI build is attributed to Reliance Intelligence. NSE-listed parent, so annual report is the T1 source.

name: ESDS Software Solution Limited
one_line: Indian managed cloud provider; contracted $1.25bn of NVIDIA B300 capacity from Sharon AI in Australia.

name: Larsen & Toubro Limited
one_line: Indian engineering conglomerate building NVIDIA AI factory data centres in Chennai and Mumbai.
notes: NVIDIA states an initial Chennai expansion to 30MW and a new Mumbai facility at 40MW, targeting gigawatt-scale over time. E2E Networks runs HGX B200 systems inside L&T's Vyoma data centre in Chennai.

name: Netweb Technologies India Limited
one_line: Indian HPC/AI systems maker building NVIDIA GB200 NVL4-based Tyrone Camarero supercomputing systems in India.
notes: Supply-side manufacturer rather than a compute seller; included because it is part of the Indian AI compute supply chain.

name: SAKURA internet Inc.
one_line: Japanese cloud operator running the Ishikari data centre and the Koukaryoku generative-AI GPU cloud on NVIDIA hardware.
notes: TSE-listed; securities reports are the T1 source for GPU capex. No public per-hour rate card captured in this pass.

name: GMO Internet Group, Inc.
one_line: Japanese internet group running GMO GPU Cloud on NVIDIA H200 with Spectrum-X networking.
notes: NVIDIA's release describes a full-stack H200 / Spectrum-X / BlueField-3 build. Ticker TSE:9449 is the GMO Internet Group listing; not re-verified against a filing in this pass.

name: SoftBank Corp.
one_line: Japanese telco building distributed AI data centres and launching an AI Data Center GPU Cloud on GB200 NVL72 under the Infrinia AI Cloud OS.
notes: Distinguish SoftBank Corp. (TSE:9434, the telco) from SoftBank Group Corp. (TSE:9984, the investor). The GPU cloud and the Sakai site sit with the telco. SB Telecom Singapore is the SEA subsidiary in the SC ZEUS / Robust HPC pact.

name: KDDI Corporation
one_line: Japanese telco operating the Osaka Sakai AI data centre and a GPU cloud on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72.
notes: Osaka Sakai opened 22 January 2026, 100% renewable-powered, repurposed from the Sharp Sakai plant. GPU cloud trials from 22 Jan 2026, general applications from 1 April 2026. No public hourly rate captured.

name: Highreso Inc.
one_line: Japanese low-cost GPU cloud operator (GPUSOROBAN) with NVIDIA H200 facilities in Ishikawa and Kagawa.
notes: NVIDIA release states 1,600 NVIDIA GPUs across two Highreso facilities. Party to the April 2025 reciprocal-GPU-supply agreement with KDDI and SAKURA internet.

name: RUTILEA, Inc.
one_line: Japanese AI company operating an NVIDIA Hopper GPU facility at Okuma, Fukushima.
notes: NVIDIA states more than 1,000 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, Okuma facility operational from September 2024. HQ city Kyoto not re-verified in this pass.

name: NAVER Cloud Corp.
one_line: Korean sovereign cloud provider deploying over 60,000 NVIDIA GPUs including RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
notes: Subsidiary of NAVER Corporation (KRX:035420); NAVER Cloud itself is not separately listed. One of three operators of Korea's National AI Computing Center alongside NHN Cloud and Kakao.

name: NHN Cloud Corp.
one_line: Korean cloud provider, one of three operators of the government National AI Computing Center GPU pool.
notes: No individual GPU count disclosed in the NVIDIA release; only the joint 50,000-GPU national programme figure. HQ Pangyo not re-verified.

name: kt cloud Co., Ltd.
one_line: Korean cloud arm of KT Corporation offering GPU capacity with domestic data residency.
notes: Only a third-party mention as one of the Korean-domiciled options for data residency (alongside Naver Cloud and Samsung SDS). No GPU count, MW or hourly price verified in this pass. Parent KT Corp is KRX:030200 / NYSE:KT.

name: Kakao Corp.
one_line: Korean internet group, one of three operators of the government National AI Computing Center GPU pool.
notes: No individual GPU count disclosed. KRX ticker recorded from general knowledge of the listing, not re-verified against a filing in this pass.

name: SK Telecom Co., Ltd.
one_line: Korean telco building the Ulsan AI data centre with AWS and targeting 15 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2035.
notes: SK Group, SK Telecom, SK Broadband, SK hynix and SK Gas all appear in the Ulsan story; SK Telecom and SK Broadband are the named investors. Also KRX-listed with an ADR.

name: Samsung SDS Co., Ltd.
one_line: Korean IT services arm of Samsung; first in Korea to sell NVIDIA B300 GPU capacity on a pay-as-you-go subscription.
notes: B300 GPUaaS launched 26 March 2026 on a subscription model; a token-billed serverless inference service was slated for Q3 2026. No published per-hour price. Distinct from Samsung Electronics (KRX:005930), which separately committed over 50,000 GPUs to a semiconductor AI factory.

name: Chunghwa Telecom Co., Ltd.
one_line: Taiwan's incumbent telco, expanding AI-capable internet data centre capacity in Taoyuan and Taichung.
notes: TWSE-listed and NYSE-ADR (CHT); quarterly filings are the T1 source. Lunping, Taoyuan facility began operations in Q2 2026 and adds up to 36MW at full build-out.

name: ASUSTeK Computer Inc.
one_line: Taiwanese systems maker; built the liquid-cooled Nano4 AI supercomputer for NCHC and co-developed the Taiwan Computing Cloud.
notes: Taiwan Web Service Corporation (TWS) is the ASUS-affiliated operator of Taiwan AI Cloud / TWCC. The exact corporate relationship between ASUS, TWS and NCHC was not verified in this pass.

name: Quanta Computer Inc.
one_line: Taiwanese ODM and cloud systems maker (QCT); co-developer of the Taiwan Computing Cloud platform.
notes: Named by NCHC as a joint developer of TWCC alongside ASUS and Taiwan Mobile. QCT is Quanta's cloud subsidiary.

name: National Center for High-performance Computing
one_line: Taiwan's national HPC centre, operator of the Taiwania supercomputers, TWCC and the Nano4 NVIDIA cluster in Tainan.
notes: NCHC headquarters Hsinchu with branches in Taichung and Tainan; the Cloud Compute Center sits in Tainan.

name: Bitdeer Technologies Group
one_line: Singapore-headquartered listed operator converting bitcoin-mining data centre capacity into liquid-cooled AI cloud sites in Malaysia and beyond.
notes: Monthly production and operations updates filed with the SEC are T1. APAC AI footprint: Cyberjaya 2MW online, Cyberjaya 9.5MW pipeline (Q4 2026 energisation), Johor Bahru 21.7MW IT (Q1 2027). Also holds 100MW at Gedu and 500MW at Jigmeling in Bhutan, both currently crypto rather than AI.

name: Firmus Technologies
one_line: Singapore/Australia AI infrastructure company building immersion- and direct-to-chip-cooled NVIDIA AI factories across Australia, Singapore and Indonesia.
notes: Founded 2019; developing roughly 1.6GW globally by 2028 per DCD. Sustainable Metal Cloud is the earlier/associated brand for the Singapore immersion-cooled compute business. Treat Firmus, Firmus Technologies, Firmus Australia and Sustainable Metal Cloud as one entity.

name: SC ZEUS Data Centers
one_line: Singapore data centre developer sourcing land and building core AI infrastructure across Southeast Asia.
notes: Role in the 1 August 2026 tripartite pact: land sourcing, design, building and operating core infrastructure. No website verified.

name: Robust HPC Group
one_line: Malaysian supercomputing firm procuring and running GPU clusters for Southeast Asian AI factories.
notes: Role in the 1 August 2026 tripartite pact: GPU cluster procurement, setup and management.

name: YTL Power International Berhad
aliases: YTL Data Center Holdings Pte. Ltd.
one_line: Malaysian listed utility and data centre developer operating the Kulai Green Data Center Park and the NVIDIA-powered YTL AI Cloud.
notes: Bursa Malaysia-listed, so annual reports and Bursa announcements are T1. YTL Data Center Holdings Pte Ltd is the Singapore-domiciled data centre vehicle; SIPP Power Sdn Bhd is the entity acquiring the Sedenak land. Kulai campus reported at 298MW contracted capacity heading to 1,000MW.

name: TM Nxera
one_line: Telekom Malaysia and Singtel Nxera joint venture building an AI-ready data centre campus at Iskandar Puteri, Johor.
notes: TM One and TM Global are Telekom Malaysia business units that appear alongside TM Nxera in directories; treat as related but not identical. Parent TM is Bursa-listed.

name: Racks Central Pte Ltd
one_line: Singapore data centre developer building AI campuses at Pasir Gudang in Johor and at Nongsa in Batam.
notes: CEO Bobby Wee. Signed a 100MW phase-1 electricity supply agreement with TNB on 22 April 2026 and has separate MoUs with renewable suppliers.

name: DayOne
one_line: Pan-Asian hyperscale data centre developer with large campuses in Johor, Batam, Jakarta and Thailand.
notes: Landlord for Firmus's 360MW Batam AI campus at Kabil Tech Park, which carries a 450MW PPA with PLN Batam. Also listed at Nongsa Digital Park NDP1-NDP3 (up to 72MW each) and Nusajaya Tech Park NTP1-NTP3 (69.5MW each) in Johor. Frequently described as the international arm of GDS Holdings; that corporate relationship was not verified in this pass.

name: PT Indosat Tbk (Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison)
one_line: Indonesian telco building sovereign AI compute; parent of Lintasarta's GPU Merdeka cloud and co-founder of the 1 GW Zankore AI factory platform.
notes: Lintasarta (PT Aplikanusa Lintasarta) is the Indosat subsidiary operating GPU Merdeka on 8x H100 SXM servers. Zankore is the new 1 GW platform with Ooredoo Group as lead investor, Nokia and NVIDIA. IDX-listed.

name: NeutraDC
one_line: Telkom Indonesia's data centre arm, operating the Nxera Batam hyperscale campus.
notes: Nxera Batam at Kabil Integrated Industrial Estate: 51MW ultimate IT load, 17MW initial phase, roughly 5 hectares, BTM-1 topped off October 2025. Parent Telkom Indonesia is IDX:TLKM / NYSE:TLK; NeutraDC itself is not separately listed.

name: SIAM.AI CLOUD
one_line: Thailand's first NVIDIA Cloud Partner, selling sovereign GPU compute and building a large Thai AI data centre.
notes: CEO Ratanaphon Wongnapachant. Registered address 1252/1 True Tower 2, Pattanakarn Road, Suan Luang, Bangkok 10250. Roadmap includes H200 and GB200 Grace Blackwell. No public hourly rate card found. The Nikkei article is blocked by robots.txt; only its headline (100MW data centre) could be read.

name: FPT Corporation
one_line: Vietnamese IT group operating the FPT AI Factory GPU cloud across Vietnam and Japan on NVIDIA HGX platforms.
notes: Runs HGX H100 and HGX H200 today, expanding to HGX B300 with availability date unconfirmed. Reported 43 AI cloud services used by more than 18,000 users; FPT group 2025 revenue US$2.66bn. HOSE-listed.

name: Viettel IDC
one_line: Data centre arm of Vietnam's military-owned telco Viettel, building the country's largest data centre at Cu Chi.
notes: Reported as operating 15 data centres with 87MW combined, targeting 24 data centres and 560MW by 2030. State-owned, not listed.

name: CMC Telecom
one_line: Vietnamese telco and data centre investor named among the country's main DC developers.
notes: Only verified as a named DC investor in a market-report release; no MW, GPU count or price verified. Parent CMC Corporation is HOSE:CMG; not re-verified here.

name: NEXTDC Limited
one_line: Australian listed colocation operator; landlord for Sharon AI and proposed developer of the 612MW S7 Eastern Creek campus with OpenAI as anchor.
notes: ASX-listed; half-year and annual reports are T1 for contracted capacity. S7 land at Eastern Creek acquired October 2024 for A$353m.

name: DigiCo Infrastructure REIT
one_line: Australian listed data centre REIT with Sydney, Brisbane and Adelaide capacity leased to hyperscale, neocloud and government customers.
notes: ASX-listed; results announcements are T1. Guided Australian contracted IT capacity to 41MW by June 2026 against a prior 27MW run-rate target, and total billed IT capacity to at least 85MW by July 2026.

name: Sharon AI, Inc.
one_line: Australian sovereign GPU neocloud listed on Nasdaq, deploying NVIDIA B200/B300/GB300 capacity in leased Australian data centres.
notes: Founded 2021, CEO James Manning. Nasdaq IPO February 2026 at US$30.00/share raising US$125m. Leases at Equinix SYD3 and SYD5 and NEXTDC M3. Nasdaq filings are T1 and should override the third-party index used here.

name: ResetData
one_line: Australian liquid-immersion AI factory operator running NVIDIA H200 capacity in Melbourne, backed by Centuria.
notes: AI-F1 at 818 Bourke Street, Docklands, Melbourne, operational August 2025 on NVIDIA H200. Immersion cooling claimed at PUE 1.02-1.10 and 100+ kW racks.

name: Centuria Capital Group
one_line: Australian listed fund manager financing ResetData's AI factory build-out with GPU-secured debt and dedicated on-site generation.
notes: ASX-listed; the A$165m Macquarie GPU bridge facility and A$300m June 2026 equity raise should be confirmed against ASX announcements as T1.

name: SUNeVision Holdings Ltd
one_line: Hong Kong's largest data centre operator, building the three-phase MEGA IDC at Tseung Kwan O for AI workloads.
notes: Subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties (HKEX:0016). MEGA IDC total investment stated at over HK$15bn; Phase One delivered 500,000 sq ft and 50MW; all three phases to reach 1.2m sq ft and over 180MW.

name: AirTrunk Operating Pty Ltd
one_line: APAC hyperscale data centre platform with campuses in Australia, Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Malaysia and India.
notes: Part of an AirTrunk-ByteDance consortium that won capacity in Singapore's 2023 DC-CFA pilot. Johor sites JHB1-JHB4 listed, with JHB3 at 138+MW and JHB4 at 142+MW. Ownership (Blackstone-led) not re-verified in this pass.

name: Keppel Data Centres
one_line: Singapore data centre developer; one of four winners of Singapore's 2026 200MW capacity allocation.
notes: Part of Keppel Ltd (SGX:BN4); Keppel DC REIT (SGX:AJBU) is a separate listed vehicle. Also holds Keppel DC Johor 1 at Sedenak Tech Park.

name: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres
one_line: Singapore-headquartered data centre platform with campuses across Singapore, Johor, Indonesia, India and Thailand.
notes: One of four winners of Singapore's August 2026 200MW allocation. STT Johor Campus / STT Johor 1 listed at 120MW; STT Jakarta campus at 72MW.

name: Equinix, Inc.
one_line: Global colocation operator; won 50MW in Singapore's 2026 allocation and hosts Sharon AI GPU capacity in Sydney.
notes: Included because of APAC supply relevance, not as an APAC-headquartered provider. Also won capacity in Singapore's 2023 DC-CFA pilot.

name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
one_line: Global data centre REIT; won 50MW in Singapore's 2026 allocation and is a Digital Connexion JV partner with Reliance and Brookfield in India.
notes: Included for APAC supply relevance. The Singapore allocation is described as provisional.

name: Tenaga Nasional Berhad
one_line: Malaysia's national utility and the gatekeeper of Peninsular Malaysia's data centre grid connection queue.
notes: Reported to have signed electricity supply agreements with 49 data centre projects totalling 7,100MW, against roughly 850MW of load actually energised by October 2025 and roughly 27,000MW of Peninsular installed capacity. RM42.8bn (about $10bn) allocated for grid upgrades July 2025 to December 2027. Bursa-listed, so its annual report is T1.

name: PLN Batam
one_line: Batam's electricity utility, counterparty to the 450MW PPA underpinning DayOne's Kabil Tech Park AI campus.
notes: Subsidiary of PT PLN (Persero). Batam operates a separate grid from the Java-Bali system, which is part of why it is attracting Singapore-adjacent AI load.

name: Gunvor Group
one_line: Commodity trading house supplying 600MW of firm power to Firmus's South Australian AI campuses under a 12-year agreement.
notes: Included as the power counterparty in an APAC compute deal, not as an APAC entity.

name: OpenAI
one_line: AI developer; signed an MoU with NEXTDC to anchor a proposed A$7bn Sydney AI campus.
notes: Included as the demand-side counterparty in the largest single announced APAC campus deal.

name: NVIDIA Corporation
one_line: Chip supplier and, increasingly, an equity and offtake counterparty across APAC AI factory projects.
notes: Included because nearly every APAC compute supply record has NVIDIA as the from_entity for chips.

name: Gorilla Technology Group Inc.
one_line: Listed edge-AI and video analytics firm that signed an AI infrastructure agreement with Yotta for India's sovereign AI build-out.
notes: Only the headline and lede of the announcement were readable in this pass; deal value and scope not verified. HQ listed as London in company materials but not re-verified here.

name: CoreWeave, Inc.
aliases: CoreWeave Compute Acquisition Co. II/IV/V/VII/VIII, LLC
one_line: The largest GPU cloud provider and by far the largest GPU-backed borrower, with $35.6bn of debt at 30 June 2026.
notes: CIK 0001769628. Formerly Atlantic Crypto Corp (filings through 2019-10-03). Registered address 290 W Mt. Pleasant Ave., Suite 4100, Livingston, NJ 07039. Borrows through a ladder of named SPVs (CCAC II/IV/V/VII/VIII, CoreWeave Financing DDTL V and V-V) — always match a facility to its SPV, not just to 'CoreWeave'.

name: Lambda
one_line: Private GPU cloud provider; first private neocloud to get an investment-grade-rated term loan B.
notes: Private — files no consolidated debt schedule, so its true leverage is unobservable. CEO Michel Combes. Commonly written 'Lambda Labs' in press but the company brands as 'Lambda'.

name: Nebius Group N.V.
one_line: European-domiciled AI cloud provider borrowing against GPUs and hyperscaler contracts.
notes: SEC CIK 0001513845; files 6-K as a foreign private issuer. Says it holds more than $40bn of contracted revenue from investment-grade customers including Microsoft and Meta available to securitise. Nvidia disclosed a stake reported at 9.3% in July 2026.

name: IREN Limited
one_line: Bitcoin miner turned AI data centre operator, financing GPUs against a Microsoft contract.
notes: SEC CIK 0001878848. Formerly Iris Energy. Borrows through IE US Hardware 3 LLC. Sites include Childress, Texas and Mackenzie, British Columbia. Fiscal year ends 30 June.

name: TeraWulf Inc.
one_line: Bitcoin miner turned AI hosting operator whose bonds are part-secured by a Google warrant pledge.
notes: SEC CIK 0001083301. Lake Mariner campus at Barker, New York. Its Fluidstack hosting agreements are backstopped by Google, which holds warrants over TeraWulf stock.

name: Applied Digital Corporation
one_line: AI data centre developer funding individual buildings with ring-fenced secured bonds.
notes: Polaris Forge 1 campus at Ellendale, North Dakota. Finances one building at a time through a dedicated ComputeCo SPV — a template other developers are copying.

name: Cipher Digital Inc.
one_line: Data centre developer leasing its Texas capacity to Fluidstack under Google-backstopped agreements.
notes: SEC CIK 0001819989. RENAMED from Cipher Mining Inc. to Cipher Digital Inc. during 2026 — SEC filings switch name around February 2026 under the same CIK and CIFR ticker. Barber Lake site at Colorado City, Texas (300 MW, fully leased to Fluidstack). CEO Tyler Page.

name: Galaxy Digital Inc.
aliases: Galaxy Helios Data Centers II LLC
one_line: Crypto financial firm converting its Helios campus in Texas into data centres leased to CoreWeave.
notes: SEC CIK 0001859392. Helios campus in Dickens County, Texas, 800 MW approved, fully committed to CoreWeave on 15-year leases. Bondholders in Galaxy's project SPVs are ultimately exposed to CoreWeave's Ba2/BB+ credit.

name: Crusoe Energy Systems
one_line: Private energy-first AI data centre developer; builder of OpenAI's Abilene Stargate campus.
notes: Private. CEO Chase Lochmiller. Abilene, Texas campus built on the Lancium Clean Campus in JV with Blue Owl Capital and Primary Digital Infrastructure. No public debt schedule.

name: Nscale
one_line: UK neocloud building sovereign AI capacity in Norway and the US, contracted to Microsoft.
notes: ALIAS WARNING: Nscale / NScale / Nscale Global Holdings are ONE entity. Narvik, Norway campus. Contracted with Microsoft for 200,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Nvidia participated in a $2bn round at a $14.6bn valuation in March 2026; reported to be pursuing a US IPO in August 2026.

name: Fluidstack
one_line: London neocloud that leases third-party data centre capacity, with its lease obligations backstopped by Google.
notes: ALIAS WARNING: Fluidstack / FluidStack are ONE entity; the US contracting entity is Fluidstack USA I Inc. Private, discloses no debt. Its whole credit story is that GOOGLE BACKSTOPS ITS LEASES — $1.73bn at Cipher's Barber Lake and $1.8bn at the TeraWulf JV — which is what lets its landlords issue bonds.

name: SharonAI Holdings, Inc.
one_line: Australian neocloud financing GPUs through on-chain non-recourse credit.
notes: SEC CIK 0002068385, warrants SHAZW. Co-founder and Chairman James Manning. Nasdaq listing February 2026 raised ~$125m gross; $350m convertible senior notes May 2026; $1.6bn strategic financing June 2026; cash of ~$1.86bn at 2026-06-30. Targeting 70-80% loan-to-value asset-level debt with NO BINDING ARRANGEMENTS finalised as of its August 2026 prospectus.

name: WhiteFiber, Inc.
one_line: Small-cap AI infrastructure operator with GPU-secured bank debt in Iceland and Canada.
notes: SEC CIK 0002042022. Related to Bit Digital. Useful as a fully documented small-scale example of GPU collateral: the Landsbankinn facility takes security over named GPU servers, CPU servers and InfiniBand switches.

name: Riot Platforms, Inc.
one_line: Bitcoin miner converting its Rockdale, Texas campus to AI leases with AMD and a frontier AI lab.
notes: SEC CIK 0001167419. Rockdale and Corsicana campuses in Texas. Signed a 191 MW, 20-year, $9.1bn lease with an unnamed 'leading frontier AI lab' and delivered 25 MW to AMD in May 2026. Subsidiaries ESS Metron and E4A provide vertically integrated electrical equipment.

name: Yondr
one_line: Data centre developer whose Yondr JK 1 LLC SPV issued $715m of 2031 secured notes.
notes: MINIMAL RECORD. Known only from an Octus listing of outstanding AI infrastructure bonds. HQ, ownership and the tenant behind Yondr JK 1 LLC are not established.

name: PolarDC
one_line: H.I.G.-owned data centre platform with EUR 750m of floating-rate debt outstanding.
notes: MINIMAL RECORD. Described by Octus as 'PolarDC (HIG-owned)'. Country, sites and tenants not established.

name: Elk Grove Village Property
one_line: A single data centre property in Illinois financed with $900m of 7.5% notes due 2031.
notes: MINIMAL RECORD — this is a financing vehicle name from an Octus bond listing, not a verified corporate entity. Sponsor and tenant unknown.

name: Flash Compute
one_line: The 168 MW TeraWulf-Fluidstack joint venture that issued $1.275bn of 8% notes due 2030.
notes: JV between TeraWulf and Fluidstack. Its bonds are financeable because Google backstops $1.8bn of Fluidstack's lease obligations to it. Legal form and exact ownership split not established.

name: Meta / Blue Owl Hyperion joint venture
one_line: The off-balance-sheet vehicle, 80% Blue Owl and 20% Meta, that owns Meta's Hyperion campus.
notes: NAME CAUTION: Meta's press release does not name the JV entity; 'Beignet Investor LLC' is the name used in secondary reporting of the bond issue and is recorded here as an alias only. Approximately $27bn of development cost; Blue Owl funds 80%, Meta 20%; Blue Owl contributed ~$7bn cash and Meta took a ~$3bn distribution. Meta gives a capped 16-year residual value guarantee.

name: Neocloud sector (aggregate)
one_line: Placeholder counterparty for market-level aggregates, not a real company.
notes: SYNTHETIC ENTITY used only by the market-size context record. Do not treat as a counterparty.

name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
one_line: Nvidia's main GPU rival, which gave OpenAI a warrant over 160 million of its own shares as a purchase incentive.
notes: AMD's circularity runs the opposite way to Nvidia's: rather than investing in the customer, it issued the customer equity in itself, vesting against 6 GW of deployments and AMD share-price targets. AMD is also a data centre TENANT — it leases 50 MW from Riot Platforms at Rockdale.

name: Microsoft Corporation
one_line: Hyperscaler that invests in the AI labs and neoclouds that then buy its cloud capacity or sell it theirs.
notes: Investor in OpenAI and Anthropic; customer of Nscale (200,000 GB300) and IREN (Childress GPU services) and Nebius. Booked $3.2bn of income from its Anthropic stake in the quarter reported 2026-07-29. Microsoft's exact OpenAI ownership after the 2025 restructuring was NOT VERIFIED in this research.

name: Google LLC
one_line: Hyperscaler whose lease backstops and warrant pledges are what make several neocloud bond issues financeable.
notes: Backstops Fluidstack's lease obligations — $1.73bn at Cipher's Barber Lake and $1.8bn at the TeraWulf/Fluidstack JV — and pledged warrants over TeraWulf stock as collateral for the $3.2bn WULF Compute notes, taking warrants over ~41m WULF shares (~8%) in return. Also an Anthropic investor. Google's credit, not the operator's, is often the real security.

name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
one_line: Hyperscaler that moved its largest data centre off balance sheet using a JV, $27bn of bonds and a residual value guarantee.
notes: Holds 20% of the Hyperion JV and gives a capped 16-year residual value guarantee that converts merchant data centre risk into an A+ rated 2049 bond. Also named by Nebius as an investment-grade contracted customer.

name: Anthropic PBC
one_line: AI lab funded by Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon and Google, each of which also sells it compute.
notes: Received a combined up-to-$15bn commitment from Microsoft and Nvidia announced 2025-11-18, valued in the range of $350bn, agreeing to purchase up to 1 GW of Azure capacity and a similar amount of Nvidia-chip compute. AMAZON'S AND GOOGLE'S CURRENT INVESTMENT TOTALS WERE NOT VERIFIED in this research and are a known gap.

name: xAI
one_line: AI lab reported to have taken up to $2bn of equity from Nvidia in a $20bn round.
notes: LOW-CONFIDENCE RECORD. The Nvidia investment is reported only by a secondary funding tracker and is unverified. HQ city not established.

name: Blackstone Credit & Insurance
one_line: Anchor investor in the first investment-grade GPU-backed loan and a partner in Nvidia's $500bn platform.
notes: Anchor investor in CoreWeave's $8.5bn A3-rated DDTL 4.0. One of six partners in Nvidia's >$500bn financing platform MOUs. Also reported by SemiAnalysis to have led a $10bn facility for a Firmus project via Tactical Opportunities and Credit & Insurance.

name: Blue Owl Capital Inc.
one_line: The most active private-credit lender to AI infrastructure, from Meta's Hyperion to IREN's GPUs.
notes: Holds 80% of Meta's Hyperion JV, led $2.4bn of GPU-backed financing for IREN, and is Crusoe's JV partner on the $15bn Abilene campus. Its Real Assets platform is the vehicle for the data centre JVs.

name: Brookfield Asset Management
one_line: Infrastructure investor lending to AI data centre developers and a partner in Nvidia's financing platform.
notes: Provided Crusoe a $750m credit facility through its infrastructure debt platform in June 2025 and is one of six partners in Nvidia's >$500bn platform MOUs.

name: PIMCO
one_line: The largest reported buyer of the Hyperion data centre bonds.
notes: Meta's release confirms a portion of Blue Owl's capital was funded through a private securities offering 'to PIMCO and select bond investors'. The ~$18bn anchor figure is from a secondary credit analysis (T4), not from Meta.

name: Macquarie Group
one_line: Australian bank named as a GPU-backed lender to Fluidstack across Europe.
notes: Announced a European GPU financing deal with Fluidstack and is the named lender in reports of over $10bn of approved GPU-collateralised borrowing capacity for Fluidstack — the latter UNCONFIRMED by either company.

name: Morgan Stanley
one_line: The most frequently recurring arranger in GPU-backed lending across CoreWeave, Lambda, TeraWulf and Riot.
notes: Roles found: co-structuring agent and joint bookrunner on CoreWeave DDTL 4.0; administrative agent and joint lead arranger on CoreWeave DDTL 5.0; lead arranger and administrative agent on Lambda's $926m term loan B; bookrunner on TeraWulf's $3.2bn notes; provider of Riot's $573m interim facility; senior lead arranger on Nebius's $775m; adviser to Nvidia on the OpenAI Ohio backstop.

name: MUFG Bank, Ltd.
one_line: The single most consistent bank agent across GPU-backed facilities in 2026.
notes: Roles found: administrative agent on CoreWeave DDTL 4.0 and co-structuring agent/joint bookrunner; joint lead arranger on CoreWeave DDTL 5.0 and DDTL 5.5; joint bookrunner on Lambda's $926m term loan B; structuring agent, sole bookrunner and underwriter on Nebius's $775m facility. If any single institution is systemically exposed to GPU collateral, the evidence points here.

name: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.
one_line: Lead arranger and administrative agent on several of the largest GPU loans.
notes: Roles found: administrative agent and joint lead arranger on CoreWeave's $2.6bn DDTL 5.5; additional coordinating lead arranger on CoreWeave DDTL 4.0; joint lead arranger and bookrunner on IREN's $1.5bn DDTL; interest rate hedge counterparty to IREN. Also named among GPU-backed lenders in PitchBook's sector tally.

name: Goldman Sachs
one_line: Arranger, hedge counterparty and one of six partners in Nvidia's $500bn financing platform.
notes: Roles found: joint lead arranger and bookrunner on IREN's $1.5bn DDTL; hedge counterparty via J. Aron & Company; additional coordinating lead arranger on CoreWeave DDTL 4.0; syndicate member on Nebius's $775m; adviser to SB Energy on the OpenAI Ohio project; partner in Nvidia's >$500bn platform MOUs.

name: DNB Bank ASA
one_line: Norwegian bank in the club that financed Nscale's Narvik campus.
notes: One of five lenders — ABN AMRO, DNB, Eksfin (Export Finance Norway), Nordea and SEB — committing $790m to Nscale's Narvik data centre, with a further $790m uncommitted accordion. Recorded as the from_entity for that facility because no single agent is named.

name: Landsbankinn hf.
one_line: Icelandic bank lending against GPU servers to WhiteFiber's local subsidiary.
notes: Lender on a $20m secured term loan to WhiteFiber Iceland ehf. at three-month CME Term SOFR + 4.25%, secured over named GPU and CPU servers and InfiniBand switches. Small, but one of the most explicitly documented GPU security packages in the dataset.

name: USD.AI
one_line: A blockchain-native credit protocol that lends stablecoins against tokenised GPU collateral.
notes: Developed by Permian Labs. Dual-token model: USDai stablecoin and sUSDai yield-bearing counterpart. Approved more than US$1.2bn in guidance and non-recourse facilities across operators including SharonAI ($500m), QumulusAI and Quantum Solutions. Isolates risk at the infrastructure level by securing credit solely against verified GPU assets rather than corporate balance sheets. Co-founder and COO of Permian Labs: Conor Moore. HQ not established.

name: MagAI Ventures
one_line: Counterparty to CoreWeave's 'Magnetar Loan', a capacity prepayment accounted for as debt.
notes: ALIAS CAUTION: CoreWeave's 10-Q calls the instrument the 'Magnetar Loan' but names the counterparty 'MagAI Ventures' under the 'MagAI Capacity Agreement'. The relationship to Magnetar Capital is implied by the instrument name but NOT STATED in the filing. $189m outstanding at 2026-06-30 at a 12% effective rate, due January 2029, after a $100m partial settlement in June 2026.

In this dataset compute contracts are booked against spacex, not xai, because SpaceX is the contracting and filing entity.

name: Alphabet Inc. / Google LLC

notes: Google Cloud is treated here as part of the google entity rather than as a separate counterparty. Notable as a BUYER: $920m a month to SpaceX for xAI capacity from October 2026, plus backstops of Fluidstack's leases at Cipher Mining and TeraWulf.

name: Amazon.com, Inc.
one_line: Cloud provider and Anthropic's largest compute supplier and investor; designer of the Trainium and Graviton chips.

name: Apple Inc.

notes: The largest AI-deploying company with NO publicly disclosed compute capacity contract of any size. Its June 2026 Google Cloud arrangement was announced without dollars, chips counts, capacity or term. Reported Gemini-for-Siri licensing of about $1bn a year is a model licence, not compute, and is excluded from the deal file.

name: Oracle Corporation
one_line: Enterprise software and cloud company; OpenAI's largest single contracted compute supplier through Stargate.
notes: The OpenAI-Oracle arrangement has been stated at least three ways - 4.5GW, about $30bn a year from 2028, and $300bn over five years from 2027 - which is the most commonly double counted set of numbers in the market.

name: Broadcom Inc.
